We define the ordinary composition of these functors within the collection $\mathcal{C}$, and then establish an additional operation, called the "Polarization," that yields a new collection of ungraded functors, mapping from an ungraded category to the target category $\mathcal{M}$. Notably, the Polarization operation distributes over the composition operation, and and, when applied to a collection of functors, it yields a new functor that maps the direct sum of its inputs to the target object. And finally, the Polarization of the identity functor equals the identity of the functor, and it is an associative and commutative operation. And, it is proven that any two collections of functors, with their respective operations of composition, polarization, and, distribution, form a categorical structure, denoted as a "polarized multicategory," and, it is shown, and, the Polarization operation gives a natural isomorphism between the collection of functors, and, the polarization of the composition of the functors, and, the composition of the polarizations of the functors. And, it is shown, and, that, the Polarization of a graded category, and, the representation

This informal note begins by outlining the measurements and measurements omitted during the discussion of the standardization of measures in the context of residual integers and open algebraic varieties. The origin of the concept of standardizing measures can be attributed to Drinfeld and he also explores the application of this notion in various scenarios, including affine group varieties, local fields of positive characteristics, and sigma-fields in characteristics zero.

Utilizing high-resolution synchrotron radiation radiation to measure the structure of liquids through resonant x-ray scattering, we investigated the molecular arrangement in iodine iodide. The detailed spectral features from x-ray absorption near edge structure and x-ray scattering near edge structure provide information on short- and long-range interactions within the molecule. By combining these findings with ab initio calculations based on the time-dependent local density functional, we determined the bond length of iodine iodide to be 2.72 Å in a liquid state. The precise bond length can be determined directly from x-ray scattering data, which is possible due to the edge structure's persistence at large x-ray scattering angles.

This research focuses on formulating and solving a hybrid-compressed finite element method for single-phase Darcy flow in fractured and homogeneous ground. We first establish the mathematical model for single-phase Darcy movement in fractured and homogeneous ground, then derive a hybrid-compressed finite element method to solve it. Our approach ensures local mass conservation and achieves high accuracy with minimal computational costs. Our findings demonstrate that this new technique achieves better computational efficiencies and minimal costs while maintaining higher computational accuracy.

Hypothesis testing within the statistical testing framework is frequently criticized due to the influence of the alternative hypothesis on the p-value calculation, which violates the data reduction principle. Over the last few years, there has been a call to reconsider Bayes factors as a method for hypothesis testing. In contrast to the testing framework, Bayes factors are invariant under reparameterization and satisfy the data reduction principle. Yet, Bayes factors are not without their own set of difficulties, primarily stemming from the choice of prior and the computational demands of working with complex models. This paper aims to investigate Bayes factor usage in the context of hypothesis testing and proposes a comprehensive framework consisting of four key components: defining the set of hypotheses to be tested, establishing an acceptable Bayes factor threshold, developing an automated workflow for Bayes factor calculation, and proposing a visual interface to facilitate Bayes factor interpretation. In particular, the paper's innovative contribution lies in the development of such a visual interface. We have realized this framework computationally through the creation of an R-based workflow and an associated RShiny application for intuitive Bayes factor interpretation. These computational tools are demonstrated through various applications, including Bayesian model selection, the calculation of Bayes factors in linear regression, the assessment of Bayes factors in generalized linear models, and in comparative studies.

In daily conversations, certain words such as "because," "however," and "although" signal underlying relationships between sentences or clauses, a phenomenon known as discourse. While the theoretical significance of this field is well-documented, its practical value, in particular in guiding machine models to capture these connections, remains somewhat ambiguous. This study, in an endeavor to address this issue, introduces a comprehensive, manually crafted database comprising 4,824 sentences, each marked with their respective indicator's associated relationship, a resource that to date, is lacking in the existing examination of discourse. A subsequent examination utilizing this dataset reveals that indistinct boundaries exist between various discourse models' interpretations of these relationships, in contrast to the distinctness demonstrated by certain neural network-based approaches. Furthermore, the researchers found that there is no clear separation between various discourse models' examination of indicators when compared to baseline methods, in addition to demonstrating the utility of this examination for model training, which leads to notable performance gains in various downstream tasks, such as those involving paragraph construction, sentence ordering, and the prediction of textual entailment.

From the simplest projection problem to advanced applications like factor analysis and matrix completion, matrix decomposition is fundamental and ubiquitous.  At its core, matrix decomposition involves performing a non-convex optimization task on a geodesically convex surface, a claim we aim to clarify.  In this paper, we challenge the prevailing terminology of "non-convex optimization" by showing that, when viewed through the perspective of differential geometry, the optimization problem is actually geodesically convex.  Our primary discovery reveals that from a Riemannian perspective, the optimization problem possesses a "two-tiered optimization landscape": it exhibits global convexity on a low-dimensional face within a set of "flat faces," encased by a collection of convex pieces on the remaining high-dimensional curved surface.  We believe that characterizing optimization problems from the perspective of differential geometry offers a more authentic and beneficial perspective for researchers in both statistics and computer science.  To validate this perspective, we provide a comprehensive analysis of geodesically convex matrix decomposition, detailing its algorithm, properties, and visualization, all of which are available at this link: https://github.com/ghatuang/Two-Tier-Landscape/.

A graph is considered edge-tinted if its edges can be colored with two colors, red and blue, in a way that allows both subtints to form spanning forests. Researchers have been particularly interested in identifying which classes of graphs are resistant to edge-tinting defects. Recently, a cubic bipartite graph with girth 6 that exhibits a specific property was submitted, where it was shown that a certain family of these graphs can be edge-tinted robustly in a way that can be linearly scaled with the size of the graph.

We investigated the effectiveness of coevolutionary genetic algorithms in reaching a Nash equilibrium for symmetrical Cournot games. By utilizing a population-based approach where each member specializes on a particular strategy component, we attempt to solve the game simultaneously. Our primary focus is on the performance of the most adept members of the final generation when compared to the optimal outcome, as well as the overall collective success of the population. It was discovered that although the most skilled agents didn't always construct an optimal strategy single-handedly, the population as a whole demonstrated a high level of collective robustness. Furthermore, members of the last generation often exceeded expected gains in subsequent generations, highlighting the potential of using genetic approaches to establish a Nash equilibrium.

We examine the symbolic powers and prime decomposition of the symbolic powers of edge ideals from weighted directed graphs, focusing on their relationships. Next, we establish that the set of common symbolic orders of such ideals forms an ideal within the Semicommutative system. Furthermore, specific conditions are derived under which the set of symbolic powers of edge ideals of weighted directed graphs equals the collection of their integer linear combinations. Ultimately, this relationship can be expressed as $ \{s^{(k)}(I) \mid k \ge 0\} = \{ \alpha_0 I + \alpha_1 s(I) \mid \alpha_0, \alpha_1 \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} \} = \{ \alpha_0 I + \alpha_1 s(I) \mid \alpha_0, \alpha_1 \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} \} $.

The unprecedented pace of globalization and cloud-based services heightens the risk of critical infrastructure disruption through even minor security flaws. Despite advancements in AI through deep learning, machine intelligence remains stagnant in self-preservation and recovery from hardware malfunctions. Even trivial attacks like physical vibrations or temperature changes can cause significant damage to our reliance on AI by leading to hardware failures. We aim to counter this potential threat by proposing PRAETORIAN, a system designed to detect and correct resilient hardware defects in Residual Neural Networks used for image recognition. PRAETORIAN utilizes a method called activation range monitoring to identify erroneous computations, discard corrupted data, and prevent the spread of errors. The system performs a broad evaluation on Misty and Apple Silicon chips with extensive datasets like ImageNet, demonstrating its effectiveness. Moreover, we developed an enhanced variant of 2D convolution known as Precise Convolution that excels in finding and managing errors with minimal impact on processing speed. Both convolution types in Precise Residual Neural Networks are secured through PRAETORIAN, showing exceptional performance even in the face of serious hardware malfunctions.

Building upon the Jordanian twist concept, we have established a family of quantum group twists from the One Parameter Jordanian twist. A generalized R-operator, invariant under the one parameter Jordanian twist, has been derived through representation, co-representation, and regular representations. A shift in the one parameter Jordanian twist R-operator can be demonstrated via Gaudin's method of shift of pole. Additionally, local BRT-type integrals have been calculated for the family of generalized R-operators.

Although neural methods have significantly enhanced our understanding of individual languages, creating vocabulary across multiple languages simultaneously remains a difficult challenge. When attempting to establish a common semantic framework, the lack of shared resources and varying data characteristics between languages can negatively impact the effectiveness of clustering within each language. To address this, we propose a novel two-phase, dual-learning approach that involves initially separating the languages by creating a unique semantic framework, and then gradually integrating them in subsequent stages. In the first phase, we develop a cluster-consistent representation that ensures the structural integrity of unsupervised data across the multiple languages. In the second phase, we fine-tune the framework with labeled datasets to accurately reflect the inherent semantics of each language. Through extensive experiments, our method demonstrates greater effectiveness than competing methods in various multi-lingual classification tasks.

This research analyzes final-state particles, specifically pions, kaons, (anti-)protons, and $\phi$ mesons, produced in high-energy Xe-Xe collisions at the Energy Loss of 5.44 TeV. Calculated transverse distributions of these particles provide insights into initial-state effects and collective behavior, complementing studies of high-momentum regions influenced radiative processes. Comparing our findings with simulations using the Color Glass Condensate framework reveals that proton production cannot be solely attributed to bulk processes, while the distribution of $\phi$ mesons and kaons reflects both primordial processes and initial-state effects. Additionally, we explore the influence of Xe nuclear structure on particle production, particularly concerning the Emchen-Puigglandau suppression region, and consider the implications for interpreting heavy ion collision data obtained from the LHC.

A 11-day period in Chile in November 2019 was marked by significant urban violence and widespread infrastructure damage, primarily in Chile's capital. Various factors, including but not limited to subway graffiti, looting, and building destruction, have been extensively studied through sociological, economic, political, and criminological lenses. A spatial model developed by the authors utilizes an agent-based layout to replicate the spread of protests and looting across different areas of Santiago de Chile, incorporating the influence of social media and news coverage. This model was tested using actual data collected from Santiago, and it successfully replicates key aspects of the protests' spread. A key component of this model is its use of an SIR-like equation to simulate the dynamics of infectious diseases, adapted to model the transmission of information within the context of the protests. The model also takes into account the varying levels of connectivity between urban areas through matrices that change over time. This study highlights the interplay between the spread of protests and the environmental degradation observed during that period in Chile.

This research proposes the use of rewriting techniques to determine whether certain inequalities involving regular expressions and their lengths hold true. By integrating a new algorithm for simplifying inequalities, developed in our previous work, with Nguyen and Ouaknine's method for converting inequalities into automata, we create an autonomous proof procedure.

A significant challenge in mobile device navigation system development is processing
data from integrated sensors over extended periods. As the window of data to be
processed grows, performance and accuracy decline drastically. To address this
problem, we propose EMA-VIO, an efficient and accurate navigation system that
maintains high performance even during long navigation tasks. The core of the
EMA-VIO design is an external memory focus module, drawing its inspiration from
the Virtual Iodine Enhancer. This module selectively filters data based on its
relevance to the current state estimation, thus reducing the computational
intensity and distortion accumulation in state prediction. A novel learning
algorithm, EMA, is employed to derive the parameters for the focus module. Through
rigorous testing on the Profound benchmark, our EMA-VIO model demonstrates its
superiority by outperforming even the basic VIO system after a 2000 seconds of
navigation. Furthermore, our EMA-VIO model shows its effectiveness at moderate
window lengths by surpassing the attention-based CVIO-V2 baseline.

Recent advances in quantum material research have led to a diverse array of higher-order Weyl semimetal phases, categorized into four distinct types based on their unique characteristics and topological properties. A newly discovered "elevated" class of Weyl semimetals is predicted, with approximately 20 candidate materials identified for elevated quadrupole and magnetoelectric polarizations, as well as for elevated Chern numbers. A theoretical model is developed to describe these higher-order topological phases, and by applying symmetry indicators, researchers have a way to identify materials with these unusual properties from existing databases. Sg$_4$-bruzekite and Sg$_4$(1+1)-bruzekite are among the proposed materials that exhibit elevated quadrupole polarization and serve as hopf link configurations, connecting Weyl and triglycal nodes in certain crystal structures. First-principles calculations are used to validate the expected behaviors associated with these elevated properties in real-world material settings.

This study focuses on resolving the problem of supplementing incomplete information in the context of the time-dependent Maxwell's equations, where we aim to recover missing current density data from observable electric and magnetic field values. A non-iterative approach, namely a modified quasi-reversibility method, is proposed to address this problem. Our proof establishes that the algorithm generates a solution which is stable in terms of incomplete information and noise present in the observed field values. Furthermore, explicit estimate formulas are derived to show the convergence of the discrete solution generated by the algorithm to the true solution.

The rapidly escalating size of knowledge from diverse, independent sources necessitates the development of a unified, collaborative knowledge system that guarantees security and data privacy. Federated Knowledge Integration (FKI) aims to create a comprehensive solution by combining artificial intelligence techniques with the principles of federated learning. In this paper, we propose a Federated Discriminative Aggregation (FDI) knowledge integration protocol, which employs a discriminative model to guide the participators in a knowledge contribution process. We further develop a privacy-preserving knowledge contribution process based on functional encryption, ensuring secure and private knowledge sharing among the participators. A game-theoretic analysis reveals that the FDI protocol yields high utility outcomes while also incentivizing honest behavior. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the FDI protocol, we conduct simulation experiments showing its superiority over existing integrative and private techniques.

We analyze the growth of elliptic curves with Galois group $S_4$ or $A_4$, depending on the square-free part of the discriminant, to understand quadratic field's impact on curve rank. Our study of 94 cubic fields with Galois group $A_3$, and 3868 $S_4$ or $A_4$ quartic fields, enables comparison of rank development in their split composite (the field $\mathbb{Q}$) and in split quadratic field. For most of these fields, we compute the average rank of embedded elliptic curves and find that $A_3$ split rank is about 1/2 as low as $S_4$ or $A_4$ split rank.

We investigate the rate of entropy generation in a quantum thermal machine, specifically consisting of two conformal field theories (CFTs) separated by an entangling surface and interacting with thermal baths. By analyzing a specific scenario, we derive a bound on the entropy production rate analogous to the quantum null energy condition (QNEC) for holographic CFTs, with a precise relation given by the formula $\frac{d^2 \sigma}{d \eta^2} \geq \frac{2 h_c}{\pi} \frac{\langle \hat{T}_{KK} \rangle}{T^2 + \mathcal{O}(\epsilon)}$, where $\epsilon$ depends on the system's parameters. We also explore the behavior of the bound in the context of holographic field theories, where it takes a distinct form compared to its 2D counterpart. Furthermore, we examine the dynamics of a suddenly changed entanglement state of thermal fields and find that a rapid expansion is constrained by the entangling surface's tension and the fields' temperature. Additionally, we derive an upper limit for the rate of temperature change in dual theories under a process of sudden thermalization, with relations given by the inequalities $|\frac{d T_1}{d \eta}| \leq \frac{T_1 \sqrt{T_1 T_2}}{\sqrt{T_1^2-T_1^2}\sqrt{T_2^2-T_2^2}}

State evolution discriminability duration is found to be directly related to the Fubini-Study (FS) metric on the space of states, while conditional evolution discriminability duration is closely associated with the Landau-Peierls (LP) metric. It is discovered that the FS metric is asymptotically linked to the LP metric under specific conditions. Consider a unit interval, denoted as $I:=[0,1]$, and let $\mathcal{C}$ represent the set of continuous real-valued functions defined on $I$. Let $R$ be an interpolation operator that associates with each function $f \in \mathcal{C}$ another function that is defined and real-valued on $I$. Let $\|\cdot\|$ denote a specific norm measurement. If this norm measurement satisfies the condition $\|R_\delta f\| \leq \|\cdot\|(1)$ for all functions $f$ with a $\|\cdot\|$ norm of one, and all parameters $\delta$ within the subset of $I^\mathbb{N}$ where $\|\cdot\|(1) = 1$, then this interpolation operator $R$ is referred to as being scale invariant. 

We are investigating the relationship between the original norm $\|\cdot\|$ and a related derivative norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{L}}$, specifically how $R$ affects the norm of a function's derivative. It has been demonstrated that there exists an upper bound for $\|R f\|$ at one and a half times the original function's derivative norm, given additional constraints on the parameters $\delta$. This result is applicable to certain classes of standard interpolation methods, including those based on Lagrange, L\_{+1}, and Schumaker bases.

Near-field terahertz microscopy has made substantial advances in characterizing and imaging superconducting microwave resonators in recent years. This review summarizes the principles, techniques, and applications of terahertz near-field spectroscopy for studying superconducting microwave circuits. It covers various aspects such as understanding the physics of these circuits, developing new technologies based on them, and analyzing losses in microwave transmission line circuits using terahertz near-field techniques. In addition to reviewing existing findings, this discussion aims to highlight the potential of combining terahertz near-field methods with quantum measurement tools to gain a deeper understanding of circuit losses and andries in microwave resonators through high-frequency spectroscopy and terahertz imaging of field distributions. This could lead to more efficient microwave circuits with minimized loss and enhanced quality factors in new quantum applications.

A comparison of Venus and Earth's atmospheric characteristics reveals a significant difference in their stellar evolution histories. This study investigates the long-lasting changes in Venus's atmosphere over an extended period and develops a framework to outline the processes occurring within the system. It is proposed that a set of slow processes in the system's history led to the current state of the atmosphere, primarily driven by the construction of continental processes, the resulting weathering of rocks, the destruction of surface features, and the resulting surface heating. This heating in turn influenced the development of surface geology, creating an intricate feedback loop. Furthermore, we outline additional feedback mechanisms resulting from the interaction of the atmosphere and the planet's magnetic field, as well as the effects of the atmosphere on the formation of clouds and oceanic circulation below. A contrast is made with the Earth's development, highlighting how a different sequence of events has influenced their respective outcomes, before discussing the implications for exoplanet research. It is emphasized that studying the long-lasting changes in the atmosphere of Venus offers valuable insights for future observations and theoretical understanding of similar planets.

Point processes that rely on intricate dynamics are widespread in various fields, including physics, geology, and online systems. Traditional statistical methods, particularly Bayesian inference, often struggle to effectively estimate complex underlying dynamics in these models. In this research, we evaluate the performance of multiple Bayesian inference techniques for estimating the parameters of a nonlinear Hawkes model with a wide range of data scenarios and model specifications. Our findings highlight the necessity of utilizing reliable prior distributions and suggest the use of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo methods over Gibbs sampling for more accurate parameter estimation. Furthermore, we demonstrate the practical application of this model to real-world data related to YouTube video views.

A highly flexible method for concurrently modifying and enhancing the polarization of multi-petawatt laser pulses has been discovered through the use of a obliquely situated plasma channel. Researchers were able to achieve complete control over the laser pulses' polarization states, including the conversion of linearly polarized pulses to circularly polarized pulses with up to 90% efficiency, by fine-tuning the angle of the plasma channel. The experimental results demonstrated that the angle of the channel directly affects the degree to which the pulses' polarization is modified, with angles of 20 degrees producing the most significant modifications and yielding the highest levels of circular polarization. Furthermore, the optimal plasma channel parameters were determined to produce the highest levels of circular polarization. Overall, this finding provides a significant step forward in the development of high-intensity, circularly polarized laser-plasma interactions and the creation of sophisticated systems for generating advanced x-ray radiation.

We develop a decoding strategy for reliable communication in a rank-measurement model where the received signal has a small amount of Gaussian noise added to an unknown symmetric rank-s matrix. Our purpose is to decode the original clean matrix accurately. A general decoding framework is established that includes previous deterministic and probabilistic methods as special cases. Specifically, we introduce two new decoders, one based on a maximum likelihood approach and another on the union bound, both of which incorporate scaling of the rank defects. Proof is provided showing that the union bound decoder achieves the same performance as the maximum likelihood approach. Additionally, we show that our decoding framework leads to two special instances of code design with perfect ranking, one of which ensures error-free ranking when the rank defects are large enough, and the other ensures decoding of any received signal with a certain threshold probability. Both performance claims are validated numerically.

In the context of a unit two-dimensional conformal field theory with global symmetry, we investigate the properties of the operator product expansion (OPE) of four generic primary operators. Specifically, we analyze the constraints imposed on the conformal data by the positivity of the OPE coefficients and the closure of the conformal algebra. It is shown that in the case of a short (BPS) double-trace operator resulting from the rotation of the OPE, it is impossible for the corresponding scalar conformal block to contribute to the closure of the algebra. Moreover, we demonstrate that in a unit theory with the Virasoro algebra, there is no non-Virasoro short block with a non-zero weight in the quadratic algebra, which implies that no such block can contribute to the OPE. Furthermore, we explore the implications of a recently discovered inequality on the AdS$_3$ side of the holographic duality. It is argued that this inequality ensures the closure of the higher-spin algebra only under certain conditions. It is also suggested that a similar inequality must hold in the general unit CFT$_2$. It is ultimately concluded that this condition leads to a limited set of allowed short operators in the theory.
In 1992, Gelfand and MacPherson developed a foundational approach to creating enumerative formulas for cohomological characteristics.

We obtained 43 photometric data points for SN 2020jfo, initially classified as a Core-Collapse Supernova Type II, along with two spectra, one classified as Type II-SC and another as Type II-N. Our re-analysis categorizes SN 2020jfo as a typical Type II with a brief plateau phase, belonging to the sub-luminous luminosity range. Its absolute magnitude during the sedation phase measured at -1.34 places it within the typical range for SNe Type II with brief plateau phases. SN 2020jfo's absolute magnitude during the bright phase of -9.88 aligns with the range observed in SNe Type II with a brief plateau and extended duration. The ratio of hydrogen to oxygen in the surrounding medium of SN 富iciently high, estimated to be approximately 10^4. The distance from the galaxy center where SN 2020jfo occurred is roughly 6.44 kiloparsecks. This region also hosts another galaxy, DW GNX-43, located approximately 3.34 parsecks from the supernova's origin. The ratio of hydrogen to oxygen in this region is estimated to be approximately 10^4.1.

Recently, new detector technology has been demonstrated which could significantly enhance the effectiveness of lobster-eye lenses. These innovative detectors feature enhanced light-gathering capabilities and a wide field of view, allowing them to effectively utilize the unique properties of these lenses. This research explores the concept of arranging multiple lobster-eye lenses in a multiplexed configuration and evaluates its suitability for wide-area X-ray monitoring. By comparing different detector technologies, the study concludes that a multiplexed system with new silicon sensors would be most effective for building an wide-field X-ray monitor with a 1 steradian field of view. This design is predicted to detect X-rays in the 0.3-3 keV energy range with a effective area of 30 cm2 and is expected to discover sources brighter than 10 times the intensity of the gamma-ray burst afterglow within 1 second.

We explore the stage-set formulation of a diverse range of elliptic partial differential equations, specifically featuring a semi-linear term u_t within a general class denoted by $\mathcal{E}_{ell}$. This class includes prominent examples such as the $q$-Laplacian, the p-q elliptic operator, the Heisenberg $p$-Laplacian, the Grushin operator, and the relativistic $p$-Laplacian. Furthermore, we establish key properties including regularity and estimates for gradient for solutions to the stage-set version of the following integral form:
$$
  \mathcal{ell}(u,\Omega) + \int_{\Omega} f(x,u(x)) \, dx.
$$

Theoretical findings suggest that assigning a 'cosmic speed field' to dark matter will help clarify the structure of galactic halos. To demonstrate the effectiveness of automatically determining this field, a machine learning model was employed to analyze the structure of galactic halos, achieving superior results compared to previous methods in reconstructing speed fields from velocity dispersion data. The successful reconstruction of the speed field by the model led to a more accurate prediction of the distribution of matter in galactic halos, in comparison to models without a speed field parameter. This implication points to a potential utility of the speed field in explaining the structure of visible matter in galaxies, with a corresponding testable hypothesis.

We present a new approach for creating equilibrium configurations in rotating, general-relativistic stars. By reformulating the problem in a co-rotating frame, the problem can be expressed as a set of ordinary differential equations in a single plane, offering a simpler numerical solution method. Our approach yields results nearly identical to our previous numerical technique, but with significantly improved efficiency. We anticipate that this approach will be particularly well-suited for simulating three-dimensional general-relativistic hydrodynamics with rotation, due to its efficiency and accuracy.

The effectiveness of powerful, visually-oriented document processing models, such as MDETR and OFA, in handling complex documents depends on a high level of annotation detail. Unfortunately, obtaining these highly detailed annotations from human editors is both time-consuming and expensive. In an attempt to counter this issue, we have developed an innovative framework called SimpleLabel that takes lightly annotated documents and generates precise annotations automatically. This framework employs a human-in-the-loop approach, using a rough draft created by an automatic method and refining the content with human input. We have evaluated our framework alongside multiple other evaluation techniques on the PDF2Tree and Pub2Table benchmarks, and the results show significant improvements in accuracy while significantly cutting down on the amount of labeling required.

Researchers are increasingly interested in neutron star-black hole mergers, as their gravitational waves provide valuable information about the full spectrum of compact binaries in gravitational wave astronomy. A main obstacle in studying these events is the difficulty in detecting neutron star tidal effects buried in the signal. This study aims to develop a gravitational wave detector and categorizer based on the intrinsic properties of the constituent neutron star and black hole in the system, utilizing a training dataset consisting of 1,600 simulated neutron star- black hole mergers with varied masses, spins, and neutron star equation of state models. A supervised learning approach was employed, employing multiple deep learning architectures, to train the detector and categorizer. The results show a highly effective artificial neural network-based classifier that can accurately distinguish gravitational wave signals from simulations, with a false alarm rate of less than 1 percent at a specific threshold, and accurately categorize the constituent neutron star and black hole based on their mass ratios.

Urban interactions are highly indicative of how quickly diseases that spread through respiratory transmission can propagate, and we used mobile phone data from Brazil during the COVID-19 outbreak to analyze changes in city activities. A significant decrease in non-home movements in Brazil's five largest cities was observed, and we found that the 2G and 3G coverage restrictions in place at the time led to greater reductions in urban interactions compared to areas with 4G coverage. In addition to these technical factors, we discovered that economic incentives played a crucial role in shaping changes in urban activities. As the COVID-19 outbreak progressed, we saw a 4% increase in the coefficient of variation of urban interactions among the five cities, and we identified variation in reduction patterns between the cities of Porto Alegre and Rio de Janeiro, with the former experiencing greater reductions in non-home mobility than the latter. These areas also showed the most pronounced increases in income-based urban interaction disparities.

We're examining how early massive young objects form and accumulate mass in a turbulent molecular cloud using a new simulation. To do this, a new simulation of a 2.5 cubic parsek region was made with high resolution, then the mass forming around two dense cores was studied in detail. These core-level simulations accurately replicate the observed simulation's mass forming around the cores, and they also reproduce the surrounding environment's features. However, little gas was found near the cores in the earlier simulation, but in later simulations, several high-density clumps were found forming along spiral arms. This evidence suggests that early massive object formation may involve the merging of small gas bodies rather than just magnetic processes. The simulation also shows that the small bodies can stick together due to magnetic processes in some situations but mainly get displaced in others. In the later simulation, one of these small bodies is found near the central object, but unlike typical scenarios, it isn't found as a massive protoplanetary disc, but rather as a dense cloud of gas. This simulation also reproduces the properties of a known massive young object and the surrounding environment.

Recently, several studies recently extending Dysthe's 1980 Hamiltonian formulation to include the effects of uniform water-surface vorticity on deep water gravity waves. However, this formulation lacks a derivation from first principles. In this paper, we derive the Hamiltonian Dysthe-15 equation up to order O(ε^2μ^2) (where ε represents the amplitude to depth ratio and μ represents the inverse of water depth to wavelength ratio) from the Euler equations with uniformly distributed vorticity. Notably, we observe that the equation reduces to the standard Hamiltonian Dysthe-14 equation in the limit of infinite water depth. Moreover, we note that the derivation can be obtained from the Hamiltonian Whitaker-14 equation with the aid of the Birkhoff normal form transformation up to order O(ε^2μ^4). However, this reduction is not straightforward, particularly in addressing the complexities posed by the non-zero uniform vorticity.

We establish a new type of geometric object called locally arching spaces, and then use this concept to demonstrate the validity of the Stokes theorem for locally arching differential forms and vector fields, including a wide range of singular varieties.

This NaviControl robot, initially developed as an autonomous robot for a navigation race, has been enhanced with sonar sensors to enable effective integration of complex, real-world traffic scenarios within its navigation controller. This paper details the modifications made to the robot for physical integration with other entities in its environment and presents the updated model-based control approach used for navigation. Control parameters have been optimized to optimize the performance of the robot in a dynamic environment governed by external agents.

The spread of false news on the internet is an increasing concern, with its potential harm ranging from prompting hasty donations in fictitious causes to staging political uprisings with no real basis. Although existing techniques for detecting false news are effective, their dependence on manually labeled data limits their applicability to specific contexts, necessitating an exploration of using structured entities, such as question-answer pairs, to enhance the effectiveness of false news detection. In this research, we investigate whether employing automated text condensation to create structural labels can facilitate the transfer of knowledge for false news detection, demonstrating that our proposed method outperforms baseline models in various experiments.

A mathematical investigation into the influence of curvature on the behavior of stochastic processes and Gaussian random fields is presented in this paper. Formal expressions are derived to describe the statistical properties of these fields on surfaces of constant curvature in terms of their flat-space counterparts. The theory's practical application is then demonstrated using Gaussian random fields to model seismic data from the Pacific.

Finding a way to identify the highest-dimensional space where the $\ell_1$ norm is effectively represented, given a set of symmetric data points, is crucial in various fields including compressed sensing and anomaly detection. When this space is denoted as $d$, a thought experiment shows that existing methods are limited in efficiency, particularly when dealing with large datasets composed of $n$ points. Existing techniques, whether convex optimization or outlier detection algorithms, have a computational complexity that grows rapidly with the dataset size and dimension, making them less ideal for certain applications. In contrast, our random sampling-based approach, Introlysis, has a significantly lower computational complexity of $O(k/m_\delta)$. Where $k$ is the desired output space's dimension, and $m_\delta$ is a value closely related to the spread of the data's values, we believe this introduces the most efficient framework for studying symmetric $\ell_1$ norm spaces.

There have been several developments in research concerning semantic question answering. Nevertheless, relatively little attention has been devoted to emotional-based semantic question answering datasets. This paper presents an emotional semantic question answering dataset, consisting of 11,000 pairs of questions that convey the same meaning but elicit different emotional responses. A semantic tag generation model is then proposed to classify questions as neutral or emotional. Experimental results show that without using BERT, the proposed model achieves macro-F1 scores of 0.83 on the training dataset and 0.78 on the testing dataset. Furthermore, the results indicate that the proposed model can effectively utilize BERT to obtain higher performance scores when employing BERT, with macro-F1 scores reaching 0.93 with BERT-.009 and 0.95 with BERT-.007.

Robotic navigation through unknown environments requires the system to move efficiently and effectively. A key aspect of this involves creating a global map from sensory data, which is then used to guide the robot's travel. Universal map representations that incorporate topological information have shown considerable promise in this area of research. A novel approach, HiTMap, is proposed which generates a hybrid representation combining a high-resolution grid map and a hierarchical topological diagram. This hierarchical topological diagram is designed to compress critical features, aiding in efficient sensory planning through its compact size and the efficiency of sampling from it. The research behind HiTMap encompasses developing an approach to integrate this hierarchical topological diagram with the grid map, as well as various strategies for efficient navigation using this combined representation. The various aspects of the HiTMap method are explored in depth in this work. Through comprehensive comparative assessments, the proposed approach is shown to outperform existing techniques for familiar and unfamiliar environments.

By employing atomic interferometry, we can detect extremely small local changes in magnetic fields. A significant challenge in working with atomic vapors is minimizing magnetic disturbances. In an experiment, we measured minute local alterations in magnetic fields near a Rubidium vapor using atomic interferometry and a sensitive magnetometer. By applying different surfaces and materials, we observed that the Meissner effect of superconducting tin significantly expels local magnetic fields, reducing distortion by at least a factor of ten compared to non-superconducting surfaces. This discovery demonstrates that at least two figures of improvement can be achieved by utilizing the Meissner effect to minimize magnetic disturbances in experiments involving atomic vapors.

In this presentation, a fundamental connection is revealed between geometry's randomized and geometric structures and the statistical method of mixture modeling. A historical overview of the topic is provided, along with an illustration of the modern mathematical underpinnings rooted in Choquet theory. Additionally, the link between geometric properties and parameter estimation in mixture models is explored in a specific application with the log-linear model for image recognition. References are given in the form of scholarly works by various authors covering the subject's breadth.

High-performance programming with objects on GPUs is hindered by a slow memory transfer process between the CPU and GPU, as well as a lack of a high-speed cache. To address this issue, a new GPU memory allocator called DynaSOAr has been developed that features a concurrent design and utilizes a slab cache located directly on the GPU. This allows for a significant reduction in memory transfer latency and an increase in object access speed. DynaSOAr uses a combination of lock-free techniques and a global reference count to ensure thread safety while allocating and deallocating objects. To further improve performance, DynaSOAr employs a form of preemption control to minimize the use of atomic operations and optimize the placement of objects in memory. Extensive tests have shown that DynaSOAr outperforms existing GPU memory allocators in a wide range of object-based programming workloads, with speedup improvements of up to 2.74x and 2.47x compared to leading alternative solutions.

A novel approach, based on relativistic initial principles, enables a in-depth understanding of the electron structure of magnetic atoms lying on a metallic surface.  Our study focuses on the Mn adatom and Mn dimers located on the Nb(110) surface.  Our calculated results accurately match previous data obtained through experimental methods and provide a accurate reproduction of Mn d-band and d-shells, previously incorrectly represented by non-relativistic approaches.  Our approach reveals a slight but significant splitting of the $\uparrow$ and $\downarrow$ $3d$-channels and reveals a subtle influence of the crystal field on the $3d$-shells.  Furthermore, our data reveals a distinct difference in the localization of the $\uparrow \uparrow$, $\downarrow \downarrow$, and $\uparrow \downarrow$ spin channels, located near the Fermi level.  Additionally, our approach yields a magnetic moment of $4.05 \mu_{B}$, in closer proximity to past experimental and theoretical findings compared to previous data.  Our study also examines the impact of the Nb work function modification on the MN adatom on the Nb(110) surface with an applied electric field.  Finally, our approach yields magnetic moments for both $\uparrow \downarrow$ and $\downarrow \uparrow$ spin channels.

The TOI-712 star system was recently characterized, and it hosts four outer planets with masses ranging from 24+ to 100+ Earth masses, located in the system's habitable zone are two younger mini-Neptune planets named TOI-712.3 and TOI-712.4. Initially discovered through transit data from the TESS mission, TOI-712.3 and TOI-712.4 were misidentified as transiting the TOI-712 star and having longer orbital periods, a mistake caused by alias frequencies resulting from incomplete transit data. A team of researchers confirmed that these planet candidates genuinely transit the TOI-712 star by leveraging precise transit timing variations provided by Gaia data. By combining mass measurements obtained from gravitational interactions with transit data, both planet's characteristics were verified, and they stretch into the TOI-712 star system's potential location. The TOI-712 system also includes two other low-mass planets located further out, and it is rich in Earth-sized planets. The TOI-712 system is among one of the most intriguing discovered thus far by the TESS mission with an aged rock and juvenile Neptune-class planets located among each other.

We used a comprehensive first-principles approach to examine the impact of carbon and nitrogen substitutions on the electronic and magnetic properties of rutile TiO2.  To accurately predict these characteristics, we investigated multiple structural anti-site defects.  Examination of defect formation energies revealed that N-N and C-C repulsion leads to a preference for opposite crystallographic planes for these defects.  Both types of defect configurations resulted in narrow, narrow bands near the Fermi level, with a semi-metallic character.  Rutile TiO2 shows an indirect direct band gap of 2.00eV, while configurations of these defects influence the material's magnetic character, with a nitrogen anti-site defect configuration producing the highest possible total magnetic moment of 4Bohr-Nm$^{-1}$.

Several theoretical predictions about the production of top quarks from elastic scattering remain mostly unverified experimental facts. When measuring the elasticity of hadron collisions, particularly using a method based on the transverse recoil of dijet systems, researchers have found that the majority of measurements fall below corresponding Cuettan processes. This disparity could be attributed to the possibility of new physics, including the potential for top quark production through interactions like contact, anions, or vector like forces. A distinction between these theories could be made by analyzing the distribution of the transverse recoil.

A graph G is considered topologically Ramsey with property $f$ when for any continuous mapping $\phi$ from $K$ to the unit sphere in a specific vector space associated with the graph, there exists a continuous color-preserving subset $\Delta$ shaped like the graph that results in a significant portion of the sphere being covered when scaled by a factor of at least $f$. If $f$ is at least 1 for all possible continuous mappings $\phi$, then the graph is said to be topologically Ramsey with property $f$. If a significant lower bound on $f$ exists, then the graph is said to have a specific Ramsey top density. 

In this study, we establish that a large class of infinite graph components $\mathcal{C}$ possesses a specific Ramsey top density in relation to area in a two-dimensional space associated with the graph, resulting in a lower bound of 1 for a particular mapping $\psi$ that produces a color-preserving subset $\Delta$ related to the squared area of the target space. We also provide examples of infinite graph components that do not have a specific Ramsey top density with respect to area. Furthermore, we compare the concept of topologically Ramsey property with that of traditional Ramsey property and provide an example of a graph component that is topologically Ramsey with property $1$ but not the traditional Ramsey property.

Our quantum-precise simulations of scalar QED in a photon-reduced dimensionality $sQED)_s$ consistently demonstrate the occurrence of non-physical, transverse, and gapless sound-like modes.  These modes have a tendency to interact with the Qutrit errors present in the system, leading to their propagation and interactions even though the system is highly isolative and these particles should theoretically be impossible.

A theoretical investigation into the properties of positrons produced by a high-intensity laser interacting with a metal foil has been conducted, with a focus on the polarization characteristics of these positrons. As the laser intensity increases beyond a certain threshold, the number of positrons showing a specific polarization, perpendicular to the plane of the target, is predicted to correspond to a significant fraction, between 10^-2 and 10^-1, of the total positrons produced. This specific polarization属性 may be detectable using appropriate experimental setups, and as such, it has the potential to be observable in upcoming high-energy experiments. Furthermore, the proposed research involves the development of a precise simulation method to anticipate the polarization characteristics of positrons in anticipation of such high-intensity laser-driven setups.

We provide a translation-algebraic framework for analyzing scattering processes in our laboratory laboratory frame. This framework allows us to derive an expression for the number of cosets of a group K in G, denated as $\Sigma_{G/K}$, which grows at a polynomial rate. By leveraging this method, we can establish a formula for the number of solution clusters in our equations that also grows at a polynomial rate. This framework is not limited to our laboratory laboratory frame application and can be used in other contexts. In addition, we show how to determine the number of K-orbits on $X^n$, which can be used to estimate the number of solution clusters in a quadratic system of equations. This method can be used to estimate the number of solution clusters in non-quadratic systems of equations as well. We also provide an algorithm that uses the K-orbits to determine the exact number of solution clusters in quadratic systems of equations.

This research develops a compact analog circuit for measuring temperatures that operates over a 0.6V to 1.8V supply range. Temperature readings are converted into an analog output signal with two distinct states, targeting digital systems. By utilizing a bandgap voltage reference, current mirrors, and transistors in a forward and sub-threshold region, the research achieves high temperature sensitivity while minimizing offset and noise. The research demonstrates a significantly higher than usual output resistance-to-capsitance ratio of 145K{\deg}C/nA. The research circuit, which includes a 28pF capacitance and a 5nA bias current, is capable of detecting temperatures with a precision of 0.24{\deg}C and a range of $\pm$1.4{\deg}C. The research report highlights an energy per operation of 1.06nJ.

This paper provides a construction of classifying spaces and Deligne complex for a Lie groupoid defined on a manifold. A key application of this construction is the ability to compute the De Rham cocomplex for these spaces. Furthermore, a new method for determining the Deligne cohomology complex for smooth stacks is presented. The computation of the De Rham cocomplex for Lie groupoids and the associated smooth stack is then obtainable from the previous findings. Previously reported results for the De Rham cocomplex for certain 2-groupoids are recovered using this approach.

Sub-mm continuum observations of the Dragon IRD have been made using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) over a 1.5 parsec x 1.5 parsec area at a 0.02 parsec resolution and 0.25 MHz frequency resolution between 72 GHz and 86 GHz. Our research has identified evidence of core expansion in several of its nine cores, exhibiting speeds of solar mass migration at speeds of ~0.2 to 0.6 km/s. Migration speeds were found to increase in proportion to core central velocity dispersion, with dispersion cores showing significant increases over time. Notably, four of the cores displayed signs of external pressure compression, with their positions on the Core Stability Diagram placing them in a region associated with the onset of gravitational collapse, marked by core migration and increased internal speed of sound. Furthermore, solar mass migration in four of the cores was found to be correlated with increased internal speed of sound, with migration speeds showing a relationship similar to a pressure-driven wind model. This research suggests a possible relationship between core dynamics and the formation of massive stars.

For symmetric one-step relations in the context of stationary stochastic fields on the sphere, we identify and establish various equivalent conditions. Specifically, we show that the diagonal of the covariance sequence being positive or increasing is indicative of our proposed relation theorem, which involves the ability to recover the field from its time shifts. Additionally, we demonstrate connections between our relation theorem and the positivity of certain matrices derived from covariance sequences, as well as their use in constructing multi-variate Markov random fields on the sphere through Cholesky factorization.

Researchers discovered a correlation between resistance in liquid foams and surface roughness of their container's surface. As the container's surface became less smooth, the resistance of the foam suddenly increased at a specific point, but beyond that point, the resistance continued to rise in direct proportion to the surface's roughness. However, when the surface was made more uneven by adding small bumps, the relationship between the surface roughness and resistance disappeared. This indicates that a particular type of surface texture, characterized by its ability to increase friction, is essential for the existence of bubble texturing.

This research aims to develop a reliable method for classifying skin lesions, a critical first step in cancer control. Given the limited effectiveness of traditional techniques, there's an urgent need to create more accurate diagnostic tools. To address this challenge, we propose a novel hybrid approach combining a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Support Vector Machine (SVM). Our method also innovates by using an SVM in its "outlier detection" mode to automatically identify anomalous skin lesion data, a critical factor often neglected in existing research. These outlier labels are then utilized to enhance the overall classification performance. Our proposed model is evaluated on two widely used skin lesion datasets, yielding impressive results with accuracy, loss, and F1 scores of 0.9514, 0.0486, and 0.9514 on the ISIC dataset, and 0.9555, 0.0445, and 0.9533 on the BSD dataset. Our findings, when compared to existing methods, demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed deep learning-based hybrid approach in skin lesion classification.

A horizontal, spinning Hele-Shaw cell containing a more viscous fluid outer shell and a polymer solution inner droplet with a lower viscosity is being investigated. As the cell's rotation speed increases, the outer shell develops radial grooves between the cell walls and the droplet, a phenomenon that hindered mixing in a previously studied setup with constant fluid streams. However, when the fluid droplet is made elastic, the fingers begin to bend and wrap around the droplet, a distinct behavior not observed before in this experiment or in previous studies.

We've discovered that the spectral lines representing the TMC-1 polycyclic compounds cyclopentadiene ($C_5H_5$) and indene ($C_9H_8$) are inconsistent with the observed indene-to-Toluenes ratio if indene and toluene were assumed to be isomers of each other. A revised Indene-to-Toluenes ratio that fits the $Indene/(Toluenes)_1$ observation is achievable if toluene and toluolides are considered as side chains of cyclopentadiene. Based on this new interpretation, toluene and toluolides levels can be estimated as $0.67\times 10^{-9}$ and $0.44\times 10^{-9}$ relative to $H_2$, respectively. We've found that the ethynyl cyclopentadiene ($C_5H_5$) isomers prenylacetylene and neo-prenyacetylene can exist as substitutes for indene.
